text:
Metro Charter Academy enrolled 335 African American students in 2024-25
Metro Charter Academy enrolled 335 African American students in the 2024-25 school year, a decline of 11.8% from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Data showed that Metro Charter Academy enrolled 421 students during the 2024-25 school year. African American students comprised 79.6% of the student body, the most represented ethnicity at the school.
The school is in Metro Charter Academy School District, with a central office in Romulus.
Metro Charter Academy was the only school in the district to enroll African American students, with 335 in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. According to the 2024 NAEP results, the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which saw a decline of just 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups also persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students. The gap was even wider for Black students, who scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
